discovery: Discovery of the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (zero-field fractional Chern insulators) in moiré van der Waals materials

nominees.name: Jie Shan
nominees.affiliation: Cornell University, USA / Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research

nominees.name: Kin Fai Mak
nominees.affiliation: Cornell University, USA / Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research

subfield: Experimental condensed matter physics (2D materials, topological and correlated quantum matter)
motivation: For four decades, fractionally charged quasiparticles were thought to require strong magnetic fields and Landau levels. In 2023 Xiaodong Xu's group, and independently Jie Shan and Kin Fai Mak, demonstrated fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer MoTe2: fractionally quantized Hall conductance with vanishing longitudinal resistance at zero magnetic field, arising from spontaneous time-reversal breaking in topological moiré flat bands. Their optical and transport measurements, built on years of technique development in transition-metal dichalcogenide heterostructures, realized a long-sought fractional Chern insulator predicted theoretically and opened an entirely new, gate-tunable platform for lattice fractionalization, with implications for anyonic physics and topological quantum computation. The discovery was rapidly reproduced and extended, including in rhombohedral graphene, and now drives hundreds of groups worldwide. It exemplifies how van der Waals engineering can create quantum phases absent in nature.
